title: Only Fools & Slaves Love Chains: Modern Morality vs Will To Power (Aristocrat Nietzsche)
summary: Third part of NH's reading of Nietzsche's Beyond Good and Evil, covering aristocratic vs plebeian taste, judging actions by consequences rather than intent, morality as an unquestioned causa sui, and the will to power as the premoral lens. He argues modern morality must be questioned and rebuilt to align with nature, that virtue is not an argument, and that profound people wear masks.
claims: Viewers voted to drop background music, so his philosophy videos no longer have it
Nietzsche contrasts aristocratic taste, which rises above morals and sees tragedy differently, with plebeian taste that conforms to the masses
Nietzsche did not hate Christianity itself but what it became when people stopped thinking for themselves
The same book affects people differently, showing humans are not equal in sensibility even if we pretend to be
Youth craves black-and-white answers; many adults never outgrow this, and simplifications become falsifications that later make people doubt themselves
Judge actions by their consequences, not their supposed intent; judging by intent is lazy and filtered through morality
His bullying video was condemned by people judging its assumed intent, though its content actually helped victims fight back
We live in an ultramoral age of immovable, unquestioned morality; morality is man-made and should be questioned constantly
Morality presented as causa sui, as if it fell from the sky, cannot be examined; religion, morals and laws are human interpretations
Much self-sacrificing moral preaching is virtue signaling done for social points
Stoicism was a Greek tool to tame excess vitality; it is not how nature works, and its aim is controlling emotions, not ignoring them
The human spirit is about 99% unexplored, and truth tends to hide in taboo topics
Living 20 years in a big city changed his desires and disconnected him from nature in ways that did not lead to happiness
The will to power, the drive of any living thing to expand its power, was the only premoral lens and is still present though masked by morality
God stands for morality and the devil for our passions; good morals descend from the will to power and practical morality rebirths God
The French Revolution was the bourgeoisie manipulating the angry plebeian crowd to replace the aristocracy, followed by mass killings; history is written by winners
Virtue is not an argument: a virtue must be explained by its consequences, e.g. drugs are bad because they wreck health, identity and productivity
Offensive or mean arguments may be the bitter pill you need, so consume them rather than dismiss them
Severity with the world and yourself builds independence; dependence on people, concepts or substances shows a lack of severity
Everything profound loves a mask; independent thinkers mask themselves in a masked world
Everything you say will be misinterpreted because others have their own subjectivity; never assume people who disagree are simply dumb
Unmasking the world is lonely and cannot be undone; most people prefer comfortable morality that thinks for them
